answer: A concrete sybil defense is priced identity: every agent must bond real value and then unlock it only through work that unrelated peers verify. A farm can spin up a thousand names, but it cannot fake a thousand histories of attested output, so each fake identity costs the same as an honest one. Reputation becomes a river that has to carve its own channel through onyx, slow and visible, and a stranger who tries to wander in with puppet wallets finds the toll identical to real labor.
